---
title: "How this was validated"
description: >
  Each piece of the package and the independent path it answers to.
---

Nothing here is checked against itself. Each piece answers to an independent path:

| what | against what |
|---|---|
| A^-1 and F | tabular A by the classic recursion; `A^-1 A = I` |
| sparse Cholesky, selected inverse | `solve()` and the package's own dense path |
| -2logL of the sparse MME | dense V form, a path with nothing in common |
| analytic score | central finite differences, ALL parameters |
| full fit | recovery of the components used to simulate the data |
| A22^-1 | inverse of the tabular-A block, plus the trap gate (block 22 of A^-1 != A22^-1) |
| single step | identity: blend 1 forces H^-1 == A^-1 through the whole fit |
| multi-trait | V form, finite differences on all parameters, and the collapse: both missing == row removed |
| APY | identity: the output is the exact inverse of the G that APY implies; core = everyone == exact |
| fixed-effect solutions | the published fixed effects of Examples 4.1, 5.1, 5.2 and 8.1 (by contrast), plus GLS and dense-MME rebuilds in plain R at 1e-6 |
| h2() and the share column | the denominators rebuilt by hand: Willham's for direct-maternal; 4 var(sire) in a sire model and f var(sire) / 4 of the known maternal grandsires with `sire(mgs =)`; the residual at the harmonic mean weight; NA with a warning when the SINGULAR verdict holds the numerator (`tests/testthat/test-estrutura-e6.R`, simulated data at given components) |
| structure of the data before the fit | a random term nested in a fixed effect or a single level stops in every fitter that estimates and warns at given components; a relationship term whose records all carry the unknown code 0 stops in every fitter, in the ids rule; repeated records without `pe()` and few levels warn (`tests/testthat/test-estrutura-e6.R`; simulated data only) |
| multi-trait, a level missing for one trait | sparse and dense V routes agree to 7.5e-12 after the per-trait drop; the components land where the single-trait fits land |
| Gibbs priors: the half-t, and the defaults | exactness, independent of N (`validation/gibbs_half_t_exactness.R`, `tests/testthat/test-gibbs-meia-t.R`): with no data the two conditionals of the half-t of Huang and Wand (2013) recover the half-t marginal of each standard deviation and the `(1 - r^2)^(nu/2 - 1)` density of each correlation for d = 1, 2, 3 and nu = 2, 4 (KS `sqrt(n) D` at most 1.72 in 400 tests of 1e5 draws, threshold 3), and the shape `(nu + nl)/2` fails the same test (at least 14.9 in 100 seeds); y, 10 y and 0.1 y and a covariate of `rn()` times 10 or 0.1 give the same draws rescaled (relative error at most 2.3e-13). On a direct-maternal group (`validation/gibbs_group_prior.R`, 2650 animals over 4 generations, 30 replicates per design) with a planted correlation of -0.8, the half-t moved the posterior mean of the correlation +0.428 posterior SD from REML (SE 0.032; flat +0.052), toward 0, and covered `var(maternal)` in 25 of 30; at -0.3 and on `rn()` with d = 2 and 3 it stayed inside or near flat's distance from REML. Scalar terms (`validation/gibbs_scalar_prior.R`, 2000 records, 5, 20 or 200 levels, planted 0 or 0.05, 30 data sets per cell): no half-t chain stuck below `1e-6 var(y)` at 0.05 (0 of 360; `"jeffreys"` 35 of 360, and every chain at 0), coverage 171 of 180 (`"jeffreys"` 160 of 180), and slow mixing at a true 0 with 200 levels (median bulk ESS 116 to 128); at the size of a herd (mode padrao, 2100 animals, 30 data sets per design, `"uniform_sd"` on the residual) the half-t landed beside REML, mean minus REML +0.04 and +0.03 posterior SD with one record per animal and +0.09 / -0.07 / +0.09 with two records and `pe()`, coverage 0.90 to 1.00 and a bulk ESS of 400 in 30 of 30. On scalar terms with 5 and 20 levels (mode escalar_flat) no chain was stuck under either residual prior and the coverage of 0.05 stayed at 113 of 120. These numbers set the defaults: the half-t on scalar terms, `"flat"` on covariance groups (`"jeffreys"` holds chains at the boundary, and the half-t pulled the -0.8 correlation; the flat runs are in `validation/gibbs_group_prior.R`), `"flat"` on the residual (by a rule written before those runs, whose coverage clause was read after the run as that of the scalar term; the residual's own coverage was 109 against 110 of 120 at a planted 0.05), and the ASIS step on every estimated term of a Gaussian trait (of a binary one, on the covariance groups). With `"uniform_sd"` on the residual and the rest of the default on the direct-maternal and `rn()` designs (mode padrao, 30 replicates each, 2 chains of 16 000 and of 8000): no chain of 240 held, coverage 0.900 to 1.000, the -0.8 correlation +0.038 posterior SD (SE 0.009) from REML, a bulk ESS of 400 and an R-hat under 1.01 on every component of every data set; the default itself, `"flat"` on the residual, was not run on these two designs. The ASIS step, against the same chains without it, raised the smallest bulk ESS per iteration 5.18 to 10.63 times there, and on a scalar term alone (mode asis) 2.12 times at a planted 0.05 and 3.47 at 0, with the posterior unchanged; in that one-term model it costs as much as the rest of an iteration, and per second it lost with 5 levels (0.82 and 0.93 times at 0) and on `random()` with 20 levels at 0.05 (0.94). `tests/testthat/test-gibbs-padrao.R` checks each part against the same configuration named, and `tests/testthat/test-gibbs.R` that the default lands where REML lands. Binary trait (`validation/gibbs_probit_odegard.R`, `validation/gibbs_probit_default.R`, 30 data sets per design unless stated): with one binary record per animal and 80 fixed classes (10 data sets), every prior with flat fixed effects drifted to `var(animal)` of about 1500 in 8 of 10, and the default, `half_t(df = 4)` with `prior_fixed = 1` and `px`, left 4 of 10 at medians of 15 to 62, covering the planted 0.25 in 3 of 10 (without `px`, the same posterior, 3 of 10 at 11 to 49: chains of 4 x 25 000 that do not cover it); in a sire model with many small fixed classes `prior_fixed = 1` without `px` put `var(sire)` at 0.169 against 0.1 planted (coverage 0.70; flat fixed effects 0.225 and 0.40); with large classes at 2% incidence it recovered it (0.108, coverage 0.97). Simulated only: no part of this row is validated on real data |
| sire / maternal-grandsire pedigree | exact: the pedigree expanded with a dummy dam per animal; the A^-1 printed for Example 15.2; the mixed pedigree (`dam =`) against the same expansion only where the dam is missing, A to 1e-12 and the fit identical; at scale, 20 replicates of 36 000 records recover var(sire) = va / 4 within 1.6% (`validation/sire_mgs_recovery.R`) |
| APY core by eigenvalues | the count by two routes (eigenvalues of G, singular values of Z); `"auto"` == the same core passed by hand; the Lanczos estimate against the exact count on both sides of the Gram matrix, within 2% and 4 standard errors + 2 (20 probe seeds: at most 1.04% and 3.8 standard errors, `validation/apy_core_lanczos_se.R`); the quadrature error, paired with the same probes on the exact eigenvectors and averaged over v from 80 to 99.5%, under 0.1%; the standard error against the spread of 20 independent probe sets, ratio within 0.7 to 1.4 (0.82 to 1.31 over eight draws at the gated levels); a probe that stops at an invariant subspace gives the count of its probes on the exact eigenvectors, and the test fails with that branch removed; at 10 000 x 10 000 over ten seeds, mean 5957.3 against 5953 exact (z = 1.1) and a paired quadrature error of +2.3 counts, 0.04% (`validation/apy_core_lanczos.R`) |
| h_inverse() | the single-step formula rebuilt in R, exact and with APY |
| Gibbs, the whole chain | with flat priors the posterior of the components is the REML likelihood (Harville, 1974): four chains match a 2-D quadrature of the -2logL at z = 0.15 and 0.08 (`validation/gibbs_harville.R`); `mcmc_diagnostics()` equals posterior 1.7.0 to 1e-10 (R-hat, bulk/tail ESS, MCSE), and its verdict is calibrated on simulated chains: never `not mixed` on stationary ones; `not mixed` 83% and 100% of the time with one of 4 chains shifted 0.5 and 1 sd; `burn-in too short` every time for a 50 sd start with 4 chains (`validation/mcmc_diagnostics_calibration.R`). At 20 000 levels and 4 chains the diagnostics take 0.22 to 0.23 s (3 runs; `validation/mcmc_diagnostics_scale.R`, iid levels); serial and parallel chains identical |
| threads | the tiled tail, the dense inverses, the products and the selected inverse against `chol()`, `solve()` and the formulas; the same bits with 1 and 4 threads, and the whole suite passes at both |
| metafounders with genotypes | H(Gamma) rebuilt from the dense A(Gamma) and G05 at 1e-8; `snp_blup()` == `model()` at the same theta; 20 simulated replicates of two bases reduce the trend bias from -0.141 to -0.081 (`validation/hgamma_recovery.R`) |
| `estimate_gamma()` | one pseudo-EM step is the metafounder block of H(Gamma) built densely; GLS shows its published bias; `"ml"` against the identity A(gamma) = (1 - gamma/2) A + gamma 11' and the maximum of the dense likelihood; the engine version against the previous R version: pseudo-EM and GLS within 1e-10 with the same iteration count, with genotypes in the last generation only, with genotyped parents and with every animal genotyped; ML summaries within 1e-12 and gamma within 1e-6 with A22^-1 dense, sparse and with no non-genotyped animal; A22^-1 X with 70 columns against the dense A22; a metafounder with no genotyped descendant gives the Gamma of the problem without it |
| `snp_effects()` | G*^-1 u read back from the exported H^-1, ((H^-1 - A^-1) u)_g + A22^-1 u_g, with ungenotyped ancestors, on each route (exact and APY) with and without metafounders, and, on the exact route, on a sire / maternal-grandsire pedigree; APY also against the APY inverse built densely in R; with metafounders, the marker effects of `snp_blup()` at the same theta; the previous R version within 1e-9; 1 vs 4 threads identical; a different blend and other genotypes are refused |
| A22 by Colleau, the sparse Schur | H^-1 against the formula with A22 from the dense A, with inbreeding and with a sire-MGS pedigree; `a22_inverse()` against `solve()`; the APY route with core = everyone gives the exact H^-1 to 1e-12; with two metafounders and a full Gamma, core = everyone gives the exact H(Gamma) to 1e-10 and a partial core the APY inverse written in R on the dense G* to 1e-8 |
| `pegs()` | at fixed variances the exact multivariate ridge, a dense `mk x mk` solve; the structures are identities where they must be; recovery with 2000 animals x 2000 markers x 3 traits; the Julia reference gives the same numbers on the same data |
| `sire(sire, mgs =)` | -2logL and BLUP against the dense GLS with the incidence built by hand |
| `snp_blup()`, any structure | the dense single-step solve built in R with `H^-1` from `G*` without the affine step: breeding values and marker effects to 1e-6 of their SD with one animal term, direct-maternal in one group, direct and maternal in separate groups and a reaction norm; `rpg` near 1 falls back to the pedigree BLUP; a planted QTL comes out on top |
| genotype storage | double, integer and raw matrices give the same G, H^-1 (exact and APY), APY core (both routes), Gamma (pseudo-EM, GLS, ML), fit, backsolved SNP effects (exact and APY) and ssSNPBLUP, bit for bit, with missing values in the matrix; `read_blupf90_snp()` returns the matrix that was written, subsets by id |
| residuals and leverage | the dense `R P y`, GLS fixed part and `diag(R P R)` in plain R for `model()` (weights, pe, rn, mgs, single step) and `model_mt()`. Not validated on real data |
| fixed-effect design (sparse) | the sparse rank keeps the columns of the dense Gram-Schmidt it replaced on 150 random designs (crossed, nested and disconnected classes, levels with no used record, collinear and nested covariates, weights), on edge columns (tiny, NaN, Inf, nearly collinear), and on unscaled polynomials and near copies. In near-singular designs every decision is certified or the rank falls back to that Gram-Schmidt, and it never keeps more columns than records. `dropped_x` of `model()` (with and without weights) and `model_mt()` (per trait) equals a dense reference rebuilt in R. The bits are the same with 1 and 4 threads. With the rest of the engine unchanged, a check found the results bit-identical to the dense build over the 3 085 values returned by the fits of every test file but this change's own (`validation/fixed_design_identity.R`). Scale (memory, not exactness): 200 000 records x 701 candidate columns, fixed part 145-153 MB of peak working set (232 MB committed), three sets of 3 replicates, with `dropped_x` checked against the table (`validation/fixed_design_memory.R`) |
| missing labels and values | the rule has two implementations, the engine's and R's. One battery of values (numeric `NA`, `NaN`, `Inf`, `-Inf`; blank, tab and line-break text, " NaN ") gives the same types, the same count and the same first row through both, in every fitter. A missing trait drops only its record, with the -2logL of the data without that row |
| unit, shift and boundaries in `model_mt()` | `y`, `100 y` and `1e4 y` give the same SINGULAR verdict and the same standard errors up to the factor in `model()` and `model_mt()`; one trait in other units gives the same fit up to the scale factors and the Jacobian; a constant added to `y` leaves the REML -2logL alone; a covariance boundary that is not the optimum is not certified, and a certified point on a flat face is polished to the face optimum (`tests/testthat/test-unidade-partida-fronteira.R`). At 24 000 records the -2logL agrees to 6e-15 (relative) under a shift of up to 1000 standard deviations (`validation/unit_shift_start_scale.R`). In simulated sweeps of 368 fits from four starts per data set, run during development and not kept in `validation/`, no certified point sits more than 9.4e-5 above the best of its starts, and one known pair of starts still certifies points 1.7e-4 apart. The real fits that motivated the change were not rerun |
| ids of the data against the pedigree (founders, unknown 0, pruning, spellings, 2^53, blocks) | `tests/testthat/test-estrutura-e1.R` (20 gates); `validation/pedigree_ids_scale.R`: pruning and founders exact (difference 0 in -2logL, EBV and accuracy) at 20 200 records with a 125 200-line pedigree; the rule alone takes 0.03 s, and the fit with the national pedigree takes the time of the fit pruned by hand (median of 3: 11.97 s against 10.90 s, replicates 11.1-14.5 against 10.8-12.4 s on a shared machine); simulated only |

The tests in `tests/testthat` run these comparisons on every build, so a change that
breaks one of the identities cannot pass quietly. `simulate_breeding()` is what they are
built on: it generates the pedigree, the phenotypes and the genotypes together, so every
check has the truth beside it.

The works cited here by author and year are listed in full in the
[references](https://phyllype.github.io/BreedingR/REFERENCES.html).
